authorship_note: Every control's text is independently hand-authored for this milestone, synthetic and generic -- never copied from any real job posting (unlike M11-D/F/G5's authentic corpora). No provenance/privacy concerns; safe to commit in full, including verbatim text.
correction_log: v1 was authored and hash-frozen first, then run against the real (unmodified) _classify_heading_line/segment_description for the first time -- this surfaced 21/44 apparent mismatches. Direct re-verification against the module's own code and docstring (never against 'whatever the parser happened to output') found the 'who we are'/'who we are looking for'-family defect rows (003, 004, 033, 034, 035, 036, 037, 038, 039, 040) were correctly authored in v1 -- those mismatches ARE the confirmed defect, unchanged in v2. The remaining 11 mismatches were v1 AUTHORING ERRORS, not new defects, corrected in v2: (a) six controls (001, 002, 011, 012, 026, 031) used the label 'NON_QUALIFICATION' (the vocabulary-family name) where the real _SectionKind enum member is 'SKIP' -- a pure terminology fix, zero semantic change; (b) control 025 contradicted its own rationale text (said UNKNOWN, field said NON_QUALIFICATION) -- fixed to UNKNOWN; (c) controls 006/029/030 misapplied the shape-gate rule (missed that a bare colon alone is a strong signal regardless of family match, and that plain-title-case without ANY strong signal needs family corroboration) -- fixed to match this ALREADY-EXISTING, already-tested, pre-M11-G6 behavior, confirmed by direct execution; (d) control 032's original 9-word heading exceeded the 7-word shape-gate cap entirely (an unrelated artifact) -- replaced with a 7-word compound that genuinely exercises the intended two-family collision; (e) control 033 only had NBSP in two of four word-gaps (typo) -- replaced with NBSP in every gap, which changed the measured outcome itself (see its own rationale); (f) control 034's expected value assumed the weak shape signal alone would exclude it, missing that the family match independently satisfies that same corroboration requirement -- corrected to UNKNOWN, matching the other formatting variants. No control's text or label was changed to make any genuine defect-relevant row agree with current behavior -- every correction either fixes pure terminology or aligns gold with PRE-EXISTING, documented, unrelated parser behavior, confirmed directly against the source, not against inference convenience. A SECOND, independently caught authoring bug (same session, before any commit): controls 015-024 (the already-correctly-working REQUIRED/PREFERRED/RESPONSIBILITY baseline positive controls) had skip_suppression_appropriate=True -- confusing 'this heading's classification is already correct' with the field's actual, documented meaning ('should ALL content under this heading be fully, unrecoverably suppressed'). Fixed to False for all ten; skip_suppression_appropriate is now True if and only if expected_heading_kind == 'SKIP', verified programmatically across all 44 controls. A THIRD round of corrections (same session): controls 008, 027, 028, 033, 039, and 040 originally used body sentences too generic to match the EXISTING, unrelated _looks_like_requirement admission gate ('comfortable working...', 'has shipped...', 'someone who thrives...') -- correctly declined for that separate, pre-existing reason regardless of the heading finding, confounding the measurement. Reworded to carry clear requirement-signal vocabulary ('5+ years of experience...'), each verified by direct execution of _looks_like_requirement before committing. Control 044's 'Must have...' was similarly reworded to 'is required' for the same reason.

schema_notes.expected_heading_kind: Gold answer for what _classify_heading_line SHOULD resolve the heading_line to, per sound general policy -- one of REQUIRED/PREFERRED/RESPONSIBILITY/LEARNING/SKIP/UNKNOWN/NOT_A_HEADING -- these are the REAL _SectionKind enum member names (SKIP is the live code's own name for what this milestone's prose calls the NON_QUALIFICATION vocabulary family; the two are the same runtime value). NOT_A_HEADING: the line should not be recognized as a heading at all, i.e. _classify_heading_line returns None, or heading_line is null because the control has no heading.
schema_notes.skip_suppression_appropriate: True iff ALL content under this heading should be fully, unrecoverably suppressed (zero claims, zero diagnostics) -- the live behavior of _SectionKind.SKIP today. False for every heading where at least some body content could legitimately be a genuine, admissible qualification.
schema_notes.body_qualifications.expected_necessity: REQUIRED/PREFERRED/UNKNOWN (reported, not scored, when the section itself carries no default) or null for a non-qualification line. Never asserts a section-level default necessity without either a REQUIRED/PREFERRED section OR an explicit local marker in the claim text itself -- consistent with necessity.py's own real resolve_necessity_hint contract.
schema_notes.body_qualifications.should_enter_assessm: True iff this line should be admitted as AT LEAST a diagnostic claim (UnparsedClaim or JobRequirement) -- false for narrative/non-qualification lines that should be declined by the existing _looks_like_requirement gate or correctly suppressed by a genuine SKIP section.
